game: LA @ PHI, 2025-09-21 13:00 ET, outdoors, PHI -3.5, total 45.5

script.base: PHI is a 3.5-point home favorite with implied totals PHI 24.5 and LA 21.0, so the base script is a one-score PHI lead in a mid total, not a shootout and not a blowout. PHI has been run-heavy (Barkley 40 carries/148 yards, Hurts 18/82) and should keep feeding Barkley if they lead late. LA, at +3.5, should throw to stay attached: Nacua (20 targets, 221 yards) and Adams (21 targets, 157 yards) are the pass game, while Kyren (35 carries/132 yards) is involved early but can lose late carries if PHI leads.
script.flip1: PHI gets up early, runs the clock, and Hurts/Barkley rush volume rises while PHI WR yards stall (Brown is already only 9 targets/35 yards, Smith 9/69). LA abandons the run, so Kyren rush yards die and Nacua/Adams catch-up targets rise. A 3.5 spread is not by itself a starter-snap blowout flag unless the lead becomes two scores.
script.flip2: LA leads or the game turns into a track meet, PHI has to throw more than the 9-target Brown/Smith pace, and Barkley's late carries shrink while Smith/Goedert/Brown and both LA WRs clear. An outdoor weather slog could also drag the 45.5 total down, but no forecast was saved.

injury_fallout: Pre-game nflverse report, not final inactives: LA G Steve Avila is Doubtful (ankle), so versus the weeks 1-2 sample LA pressure should rise, Kyren efficiency should fall, and quick throws should tick up (Higbee 4 targets/37 yards, Kyren 4 targets/17 yards, Nacua's YAC role) while Adams' deep air (208 air yards on 21 targets, only 157 rec yards) is the piece most at risk. LA TE Colby Parkinson is Questionable (shoulder); if he sits, the bump is tiny (2 targets, -6 yards) toward Higbee and Davis Allen (3 targets/21 yards), not a Higbee 37.5 edge, and he may play. LA DE Braden Fiske is Questionable (oblique); if he sits, PHI's protection and Barkley/Hurts efficiency get a small backup-DE bump, unconfirmed. PHI QB Tanner McKee Questionable (thumb) does not change Hurts. PHI RB Will Shipley is Out (oblique): he had only 3 carries/26 yards, Dillon is next man (6/29), and Barkley already owns the lead share, so this is not a Barkley usage spike. Hurts (18/82) is the real second rusher. No snap-limit note on Nacua, Adams, Kyren, or Barkley.

matchup.shell: No coverage chart in the pack, so MOFO/MOFC and man vs zone are unknown. Known shells are blitz-only: PHI blitzes 29% and LA EPA/db is better vs blitz (0.29) than vs no blitz (0.12); LA blitzes 27% and PHI EPA/db is worse vs blitz (-0.23) than vs no blitz (0.25).
matchup.pressure: PHI's 29% blitz does not profile as a Nacua/Adams suppressor because LA's EPA is higher when blitzed. LA's 27% blitz does profile as a Hurts suppressor and should push PHI toward checkdowns (Barkley 7 targets/30 yards, Goedert 7/44) and away from deep WR yards. Avila Doubtful is the extra LA pressure source and is not in the two-game averages.
matchup.bleeds: PHI pass D is stingy left (4.85 YPA on 27 att) and softer middle (6.93 on 15) and right (7.0 on 20). PHI rush D allows 5.00 YPC and 6 runs of 10+. LA pass D bleeds left (7.35 YPA on 26 att), is fine right (4.92 on 26) and middle (5.5 on 8), and allows 4.21 YPC with 5 runs of 10+. Both sides have allowed 5 passes of 20+ (PHI 5/64, LA 5/68).
matchup.overlap: LA's co-primary is Nacua, the YAC/intermediate piece (221 rec yards on 166 air yards, 20 targets), which maps to PHI's softer middle/right rather than the 4.85 left side. Adams has more air (208) and less production (157), a worse fit if Avila cuts deep shots. PHI's top option is Barkley on the ground, and LA's rush D (4.21 YPC) is not the weak spot; LA's weak spot is left-side pass, which PHI has barely used (Brown 35 yards on 67 air, Smith 69 on 108 air).

Adams 51 and 106 on 21 targets is volatile and inefficient vs 208 air yards. Kyren rush yards 66 and 66, exactly a half-yard under 66.5, with Corum mixing in 6 carries/46 yards (2 and 44). Barkley rush 60 and 88 around 74.5, plus rec 24 and 6; Hurts has already taken 18 carries/82 yards. Brown 8 and 27 (line 17.5) and Smith 16 and 53 (line 34.5) show a run-first PHI pass game, not a WR trend. Higbee 37 yards on 4 targets in a 1-game stand-in; Goedert 44 on 7 targets. Dotson 4 targets/63 yards is efficient but has no listed prop.

edge_players.edge_sentence: Nacua is LA's YAC/middle option (221 yards on 166 air yards and 20 targets) and PHI's relative soft spots are the middle (6.93 YPA) and right (7.0), while a +3.5 dog script and LA's better EPA vs PHI's 29% blitz (0.29 vs 0.12) should keep his targets at or above the 10-per-game pace that produced the 110.5 stand-in.
edge_players.must_be_true: Nacua plays a full route share with no late scratch, LA stays in pass mode because PHI leads or the game stays within one score, and his targets stay in the middle/slot rather than being shaded exclusively to PHI's 4.85-YPA left side. Avila's absence, if he sits, must show up as quick throws to Nacua rather than as a sack-killed drive total.
edge_players.kills_it: LA leads and runs (flip 2), PHI takes the slot away, Avila's downgrade cuts dropbacks enough that a 91-yard game repeats, or the 21.0 team total simply does not support another 111-plus yard day. One bracket plus a quiet red zone loses a number this high.

pre_mortem: It's Monday and Nacua under 110.5 lost the ticket. PHI led about a field goal, Stafford did not need a 40-attempt chase, and Avila's ankle either limited him or the interior leaks became sacks that cut drives. PHI shaded the slot toward the stingy left side (4.85 YPA on 27 throws), so Nacua's looks were the 91-yard kind, not the 130-yard kind, while Adams took the one right-side explosive. A 110.5 yardage bar against a 21.0 team total was the average of two games, not a number the script had to clear, and there was no price edge to justify laying it. The middle split is only 15 attempts, so the 'bleed' can be noise.
slip_story: One-story stack would be PHI leads and runs, LA throws (Nacua recyds over with a favorite RB rush). Barkley rush over 74.5 was not added: LA allows 4.21 YPC, Hurts has already taken 18 carries/82 yards, and the 60/88 split sits on 74.5, so the counter is stronger. Dillon was the Shipley sleeper and was not added (3-carry vacuum). No PHI WR over, no total under, and no Adams under in the same slip. Single flagged lean only; no bet placed.
